preconditions.description: The input strings s and t must both have length n.

preconditions.expression: all(c in '01' for c in s) and all(c in '01' for c in t)
preconditions.description: Both s and t must be binary strings (only contain '0' and '1').
The length n must be between 1 and 1,000,000 (inclusive).

postconditions.description: The output is either '-1' (impossible) or a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of operations (0 to n).

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' if any(s[i] != t[i] for i in range(n) if s[i] != t[i] and (s[i] == '1' and t[i] == '0')) else True
postconditions.description: If there exists any position where s has '1' and t has '0', it is impossible to convert s to t, so output '-1'.

postconditions.expression: stdout == str(min_operations) if (min_operations := min_rotations(s, t)) is not None else '-1'
postconditions.description: The output is the minimum number of operations required to convert s to t, or '-1' if impossible. The function min_rotations(s, t) computes this value.
